title: The local-ladder effect: Social status and subjective well-being
central_claims: Sociometric status predicts and causally affects wellbeing more strongly than socioeconomic status.

source_manifest.title: Many Labs2: Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Samples and Settings
source_manifest.finding: High versus low sociometric-status comparison priming did not improve wellbeing in N=6905,d=-.04,95%CI[-.09,.004]. The manipulation, not every status/wellbeing association, is challenged.

source_manifest.title: Status and subjective well-being: A conceptual replication and extension of Anderson et al.(2012)
source_manifest.finding: Original author Anderson and Hildreth obtain positive causal effects with a different status-feedback manipulation;they acknowledge the original ML2failure.
